texts: The aortic and mitral valves are joined by fibrous tissue: parts of the left and the non-coronary cusps are in continuity with the anterior mitral leaflet: C.
In the picture, the white silk curtain hangs from the left salsa bowl and the empty one down to the front leaf of the mitre.
This aortomitral curtain is why endocarditis, calcification and surgery of one valve so often involve the other.
The right coronary cusp, the right bowl on brick, sits over the muscular septum, not over the mitral valve.
The semilunar valves form early, by about the ninth week, not in the twelfth, and their leaflets are layered tissue rich in collagen, elastin and glycosaminoglycans.
Memory hook: the silk curtain hangs from the left bowl and the empty bowl down to the mitre.
